author: reek
body: Phase 0a spike for Lens, the governed analytics platform. Proves the native analytics substrate: a tiny star schema lives in Codex DB, and a hand-written relational-algebra aggregation answers a business question with known numbers. The fact table is orders; the dimensions are users and products. The question is revenue by user city: a many-to-one hash join from orders to users on user-id, projection to (city, amount), then group-and-sum through the volcano executor. Every printed number is hand-computed in the seed data below.

author: reek
body: The join is many-to-one from the orders fact to the users dimension, so no fan-out is possible and a direct group-and-sum after the join is grain-correct. The hash join builds on the small users side and probes with orders; each merged row carries the order amount and the buyer's city. The merged rows are projected to (city, amount) with the relational-algebra projection, loaded into a result table, and the final aggregation and sort run through the executor. The sort is ascending in CCE code order, and CCE assigns letters by frequency (etaoinshrdlcumwfgypbvkjxqz), not alphabetically, therefore Shelbyville sorts before Capital City. The expected sidecar pins that collation.
